To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the calcineurin pathway is activated in hypertrophic hearts, that calcineurin is a necessary component of the hypertrophic response in vitro, and that calcineurins are activated by Ca2+, which is elevated in hypertrophic hearts.
the calcineurin pathway is activated in cardiac hypertrophy and that this activation is required for hypertrophy to proceed.

the calcineurin/NFAT signaling pathway is involved in the hypertrophic response to pressure overload, that this response is mediated at least in part by the induction of the fetal cardiac isoform β-MHC, and that the pathway is also involved in the hypertrophy that follows loss of myocardium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which myocytes adapt to increased work and with the transition to decompensation and heart failure.

the mechanisms that control myocyte growth in the intact organism, with the goal of understanding the mechanisms that allow physiological growth to proceed and those that lead to decompensated hypertrophy.
the mechanisms of the adaptive hypertrophic response, and the factors that determine whether the response is maladaptive or not.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hypertrophy is a normal response to increased workload that may become maladaptive if the stimulus persists or is excessive.
the hypertrophic state, in the long term, may be maladaptive, with increased risk of heart failure and death.
hypertrophy is a complex adaptive process that is beneficial in the short term but maladaptive in the long term.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hypertrophic response is a highly complex and integrated process that involves a wide variety of cell signaling pathways.
the CaMKII signaling pathway is involved in the hypertrophic response of the myocyte, and that the CaMKIIs are involved in the transition from physiological to decompensated hypertrophy.

the calcineurin-NFAT pathway plays an important role in the early stages of hypertrophy, and that calcineurin inhibitors are effective in the prevention of hypertrophy and heart disease, at least in the shorter-term.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hypertrophic response is a complex one and that the mechanisms of hypertrophy are not necessarily uniform across all cell types.
, in the longer term, cardiac hypertrophy is an inherently pathological process that can be prevented by inhibiting the calcineurin pathway.
calcineurin is a critical regulator of cardiac myocyte hypertrophy, and that its activation by Ca2+ influx through voltage-gated Ca2+ channels is a key event in the hypertrophic process.
